prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian region ATFM+A-CDM. Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport (own authority). Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. System: Regional Flow Platform alias Cedarbell (coordination only). Planning: Demand Prediction Service alias Marlinstone, Capacity Assessment Module, Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal, Digital Briefing Room. Tactical: Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, Contingency Operations Console. Integration: Weather Ingest Gateway alias Orchard, Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter, Alert Distribution Hub. Governance: Performance Analytics Warehouse, Audit Event Ledger, Identity Access Service, Business Rules Registry, Time Synchronization Service, Collaborative Decision Log. Components: North/South Runway Meter, East/West Apron Sensor, Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector, Common Situation Display. Actors: Regional Flow Manager alias Copperfin (owns intent; reviews Airport Capacity Plan, Ground Delay Program status, Tactical Regulation Proposal; chairs checkpoints, authorizes flow-measure changes when capacity mismatch); Airspace Sector Planner; Slot Coordinator (Calculated Takeoff Time, Business Rules Registry parameters); Airline Operations Coordinator (Flight Intent Message); Aircraft Operator Representative; Network Operations Liaison (Collaborative Decision Log); Meteorology Briefing Officer (Storm Cell Snapshot; Normal→Adverse Weather triggers); Airport Duty Manager (escalation); Tower Supervisor (Runway Inspection Note); Ramp Control Lead; Ground Handling Dispatcher; Handling Resource Planner; Deicing Coordinator (winter advice); Military Airspace Liaison (alerts Copperfin of routing constraints); Emergency Response Coordinator (mandatory escalation on safety/security/emergency events); Data Governance Steward (decisions in Audit Event Ledger with Time Synchronization Service timestamps); System Support Engineer (technical escalation). Flows: Flight Data Exchange→filed flights/Flight Intent Message (primary intent indicator)→Demand Prediction Service, compared with Airline Interface Adapter schedule→demand forecast. Sector Load Monitor→airspace demand indicators. Orchard normalizes weather→Capacity Assessment Module (+Airport Capacity Plan)→Airport Acceptance Rate feasibility, Ground Delay Program test. Slot Allocation Engine feasibility only. Departure Metering Service/Arrival Regulation Console only under accountable roles; outputs shown on Common Situation Display. End of period: decisions/issues→Performance Analytics Warehouse→Post Operations Report.

New part:
S108: The Weather Ingest Gateway accepts aviation forecasts, radar-derived precipitation fields, lightning alerts, wind forecasts, ceiling and visibility forecasts, and runway condition weather inputs from approved sources.
S109: Each weather feed is checked for source identity, issue time, valid time, spatial reference, and unit consistency before it is made available to the Regional Flow Platform.
S110: The Time Synchronization Service provides the reference clock used to compare forecast issue times with operational decision times.
S111: When a forecast product arrives late or fails validation, the Weather Ingest Gateway marks the feed as degraded rather than silently excluding it from the operational picture.
S112: The Meteorology Briefing Officer reviews degraded weather inputs when they affect capacity assumptions for the next planning period.
S113: Weather impacts are translated into capacity modifiers for runway configuration, arrival spacing, departure spacing, surface movement constraints, and approach sector availability.
S114: The North Runway Meter and South Runway Meter receive runway-specific capacity values after the Capacity Assessment Module applies the current wind, visibility, and precipitation assumptions.
S115: Surface constraints from the East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor are correlated with weather-driven taxi speed assumptions before the Ramp Movement Board is updated.
S116: The Airport Duty Manager may request a manual capacity review when local observations differ materially from the automated weather interpretation.
S117: The Regional Flow Manager uses the Common Situation Display to compare forecast demand, assessed capacity, and any active Ground Delay Program effects in one operational view.
S118: Forecast confidence is recorded as a confidence class, a probability value where provided by the source, a valid time range, and the forecast horizon used for the calculation.
S119: The confidence record also stores the originating feed, the processing time, the transformation version, and any manual override applied by the Meteorology Briefing Officer.
S120: Low-confidence weather forecasts remain visible to users, but the Capacity Assessment Module flags the associated capacity values as provisional.
S121: When confidence decreases below the configured threshold, the Alert Distribution Hub notifies the Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, and Airline Operations Coordinator that the capacity picture may change.
S122: All forecast confidence changes, feed quality changes, and capacity recalculations are written to the Collaborative Decision Log with synchronized timestamps.
S123: The Audit Event Ledger retains the trace from incoming forecast product to capacity value so that the Performance Analytics Warehouse can reconstruct the decision basis after operations.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
